Statute of Limitations in Filing a Greeley Car Accident Claim

Colorado law gives injured drivers a set amount of time to take legal action after a crash. For most car accident injury claims in Greeley, that window is three years from the date of the collision under

, and the same deadline applies to claims for vehicle damage. Once that window closes, courts will almost always reject the case regardless of how strong the evidence is. Certain circumstances, such as cases involving a minor, a government vehicle, or injuries that were not immediately apparent, may affect how the deadline is calculated.

Three years sounds like a long time, but it goes faster than most people expect. Photos get deleted, witnesses move on, and the other driver’s insurance company starts building its defense right away. The sooner you speak with a
Greeley car accident lawyer
, the more options you have and the stronger your case will be.
Types of Car Accidents

Not all car accidents happen the same way, and the type of collision often determines the injuries involved, the evidence available, and how liability gets established. Greeley’s busiest corridors, including the intersections near 23rd Avenue, Highway 34, and heavily traveled portions of US-85, see a wide range of serious crashes every year.
The most common types we handle include the following:
Rear-End Collisions:

These crashes happen frequently on congested stretches of US-34, where distracted or tailgating drivers fail to stop in time. Even moderate-speed impacts can cause lasting neck and back injuries, and fault is not always as straightforward as it seems.
Head-On Collisions
Often caused by impaired driving, wrong-way travel, or a driver crossing the center line, head-on crashes tend to produce the most severe injuries and the most complex liability questions.
T-Bone (Side-Impact) Collisions
Common at Greeley intersections where left-turn conflicts arise, these crashes are particularly dangerous because the side of a vehicle offers very little protection against a direct impact.
Rollover Accidents:
More likely on highway corridors and in taller vehicles like SUVs and trucks, rollovers can involve questions about road conditions, vehicle defects, and driver behavior.
Hit-and-Run Accidents
When a driver flees the scene, the window to preserve evidence closes quickly. Uninsured motorist coverage often becomes the primary recovery path when the at-fault driver cannot be identified.
Multi-Vehicle Pileups:
Chain-reaction crashes create complex liability questions across multiple drivers and insurance policies, requiring thorough investigation to identify every responsible party.
No matter what type of collision you were involved in, understanding who bears responsibility is the foundation of every claim.
Common Greeley Car Accident Injuries

The injuries produced by Greeley car accidents range from painful but recoverable to life-altering and permanent. Understanding the full scope of an injury, including how it will affect a person weeks and months from now, is central to calculating a fair claim value.
Common injuries in these cases may include:
Whiplash
and Soft Tissue Injuries:
These injuries are often brushed off as minor, but chronic neck and back pain from a crash can limit daily activity for months or longer.
Traumatic Brain Injuries
A concussion or more serious brain injury can happen in any collision where the head strikes a surface or snaps forward and back suddenly.
Spinal Cord Injuries
Herniated discs and spinal damage can require surgery and lengthy recovery, and in serious cases lead to permanent limitations in movement and function.
Broken Bones:
Fractures to the ribs, arms, legs, and pelvis are common in higher-speed crashes and often need surgical treatment before the healing process can begin.
Internal Injuries:
Organ damage from blunt force impact is not always obvious at the scene, which is why getting a full medical evaluation after any significant crash is so important.
Psychological Trauma:
Anxiety, post-traumatic stress, and depression after a serious crash are real injuries that affect daily life and deserve full recognition in any compensation claim.
The severity of an injury directly affects the value of a claim, which is why documenting injuries early and completely is one of the most important steps an injured person can take.
Steps to Take After a Car Accident in Greeley
After a crash, the first things to take care of are calling 911 and getting checked out by a doctor, even if you feel fine in the moment. Under

, drivers involved in injury-causing collisions are required to remain at the scene and exchange information with all parties. Some injuries do not show up right away, and having a medical record from the start protects both your health and your claim.
Once the immediate situation is handled, one of the most important calls you can make is to a
Greeley car accident lawyer

before speaking with any insurance company. Insurers move quickly after a crash, and anything you say without legal guidance can be used to reduce what you are owed. Evidence fades, witnesses become harder to reach, and early mistakes can be difficult to correct later. Getting legal help early keeps your options open and puts you in a much stronger position from the start.
Who Can Be Held Liable After a Greeley Car Accident?

Liability in a car accident does not always fall on a single person. Depending on how the crash happened, multiple parties may share responsibility, and identifying all of them is critical to recovering full compensation. Potentially liable parties in a Greeley car accident case include:
The at-fault driver, whose negligence, distraction, impairment, or reckless behavior caused the crash
An employer, if the driver was on the job at the time of the collision, under the legal principle of vicarious liability
A vehicle manufacturer, if a defective part such as faulty brakes, a tire blowout, or a malfunctioning safety system contributed to the crash
A government entity, if a poorly maintained road, missing signage, or a defective traffic signal created dangerous conditions
A cargo loader or trucking company, in cases where improperly secured loads or federal safety violations played a role
Determining who bears responsibility is not always straightforward, and insurance companies routinely dispute liability to reduce their exposure. Under

, Colorado’s modified comparative negligence rule allows recovery even when a victim shares some degree of fault, as long as their share stays below 50 percent. A thorough investigation from the start ensures no responsible party is overlooked and no available insurance policy goes unclaimed.
Types of Compensation We Can Help You Receive

Compensation in a car accident claim is designed to account for the full impact of the crash, not only the immediate medical bills. Colorado law recognizes both economic and non-economic losses, and an experienced attorney ensures that neither category is shortchanged during negotiations with an insurance carrier.
Economic damages cover losses with a specific dollar value:
Medical expenses, including emergency care, hospitalization, surgery, and follow-up treatment
Future medical costs for ongoing care, therapy, or assistive devices
Lost wages from time missed at work during recovery
Reduced earning capacity when injuries prevent a return to prior employment
Property damage for vehicle repair or replacement
Non-economic damages reflect the personal toll of the injury:
Physical pain and suffering
Emotional distress and mental anguish
Loss of enjoyment of life
Permanent scarring or disfigurement
In cases involving particularly reckless or willful conduct, punitive damages may also be available under Colorado law. At
Dormer Harpring

Greeley car accident lawyers

faqs.question: What should I do immediately after a car accident in Greeley?

children.text: Call 911, seek medical care right away, document the scene, and contact a
Greeley car accident lawyer
before speaking with any insurer.

faqs.question: What if the other driver does not have insurance?

children.text: Your own uninsured motorist coverage may apply. An attorney can identify all available sources of recovery and help you pursue them.

faqs.question: Can I still receive compensation if I was partially at fault for the accident?

children.text: Yes, under Colorado’s modified comparative negligence rule, you may recover damages as long as your share of fault stays below 50 percent.

faqs.question: Will I have to go to court for my car accident claim?

children.text: Most claims resolve before trial. If a fair offer is not made,
Dormer Harpring
is fully prepared to litigate on your behalf.
